title: I love my tight knit family ❤️ #Falsettos #falsettosmusical #MusicalT...
transcript: The 2016 Falsettos revival might just be a perfect production of a perfect musical. And so to get a chance to revisit it 10 years later at Carnegie Hall is an experience I will never forget. But first, I had to endure the craziest merch line I have ever seen. It took me about 45 minutes to get through the entire line. I did almost miss the start of the show, but I got this gorgeous signed poster, so totally worth it. And then it was time for the concert itself. And what can I say, Besides the fact that it was absolutely perfect? the chemistry that this cast has together is just electric. And you could tell that they were all relishing being back together again. One of the cool things about the way that this was staged is the full cast was basically on stage the entire time, and so you got to watch them watch each other with pride on their faces. It was so sweet. I should also note that this concert presentation was directed and choreographed by Ellenore Scott, and I thought she did a really great job at making it feel familiar and yet fresh. And there were so many fun New Line readings, like the way that Betsy Wolfe said, “it's so good, you'll think it's Italian.” Killed me. I will say I was doing a very good job at not crying. But then Anthony Rosenthal came out for Jason's bar mitzvah. Literally Becoming a man. And I just started sobbing and pretty much stopped through the rest of the show. Obviously, because he's much older now, his voice has changed. He couldn't do the role of Jason for this concert, so I was very glad that they were able to build in this moment for him. It was just so sweet. And, like, when Christian started singing about how proud of him he was, tears! the entire night was just so special and definitely something that I will remember for the rest of my life. And I still think Stephanie J. Block should have won the Tony. Sorry, not sorry.
